%1$s. The kill switch blocks traffic outside the VPN while FreeTunnel reconnects. Disconnect to use the network without VPN.
Unsupported rules from an older preview were removed. Review your routing rules.
Rules in the selected configuration: %1$s. These also affect routing and the full VPN fallback.
Version %1$s is verified. Tap this line to install it. If Android asks, allow installs from FreeTunnel, then tap this line again.
Waiting for Android installation confirmation… If its window closed, tap this line to start it again.
Couldn’t reach GitHub, or the download was interrupted. Check your connection and try again.
couldn’t reach GitHub, or the download was interrupted. Check your connection and try again.
GitHub is limiting update checks for now. The limit is shared by everyone on the same internet address, such as the same Wi-Fi or mobile network. Try again later.
The update failed the security check and was deleted; nothing was installed.
the update failed the security check and was deleted; nothing was installed.
Android didn’t install the update. Try again.
This build doesn’t come from the official channel, so it doesn’t update itself. Install an official release from GitHub to get updates.

Installing replaces FreeTunnel, so the VPN and its kill switch are off until FreeTunnel reconnects after the update. Until then apps go online without the VPN, unless Android blocks connections without VPN.
Allow FreeTunnel to install apps in Android’s settings (on some TVs: Security & restrictions › Unknown sources), then tap the update line in Settings again.
This device has no file picker. Paste a link from the clipboard, or create the configuration manually.
This device has no Android screen for allowing VPN connections, so FreeTunnel can’t connect.
Scan the code or open the address on a phone on the same network, and send links or TOML files. Each one is confirmed here.
This device has no home network address for a phone to reach. Connect it to Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
Couldn’t receive from a phone. Try again.
Nothing arrived in 5 minutes. Open Receive from phone again for a new code.
Receiving stopped after 5 minutes. Open Receive from phone again to send more.
A wrong code was sent 3 times, so receiving stopped. If that wasn’t you, someone else on this network tried to send a configuration. Open Receive from phone again for a new code.
This TV has no file picker. Use Receive from phone, or create the configuration manually.
Paste a tt:// link or a TrustTunnel TOML file
Or choose a TOML file, or a text file with a tt:// link
The TV shows what it received and asks before adding it. The text crosses your network unencrypted, so send it only over a network you trust.
Sent. Confirm it on the TV. You can send another below.
The TV took nothing. Paste a link or a TOML file, or choose a file, but not both, and send again. A file must be UTF-8 text: a TOML file, or a text file with a tt:// link.
The TV took nothing: that was over 512 KiB, far more than a link or a TOML file. Choose the TOML file, or the text file with the tt:// link, and send again.
The TV already has 10 waiting. Confirm them on the TV, then send again.
Wrong code. Check the address the TV shows, and try again.
Wrong code again, so the TV stopped receiving. Open Receive from phone on the TV again for a new address.

"Not a valid domain or subnet: %1$s. A subnet ending in /0 is every address: under “Bypass VPN” it would take all of its traffic out of the tunnel."

"“%1$s” uses the profile “%2$s”, which has no rules that can be used, so \"Through VPN\" would send nothing through the tunnel. The full tunnel stays on until that profile has a rule that can be used."
"Add a rule to use \"Through VPN\" — with an empty list nothing would go through the tunnel, so the full tunnel stays on."
"“%1$s” uses the profile “%2$s”, which lists both applications and domains. Android cannot send both through the tunnel at once, so the full tunnel stays on. Keep rules of one kind in that profile."
